t: On-Chain AML: Clustering and Risk-Scoring Blockchain Addresses
e: Cluster and risk-score blockchain addresses for on-chain AML and sanctions exposure.

t: Delivery-versus-Payment: Settling Securities on T+2 Without Principal Risk
e: Settle securities delivery-versus-payment on T+2 through a central securities depository — the securities analog to FX PvP.

t: Booking and Revaluing FX Forwards and Swaps for Hedging
e: Book and revalue FX forward contracts and swaps for hedging, beyond spot conversion.

t: Building a Cash-Flow Forecasting Pipeline for Treasury
e: Project liquidity positions from known and predicted flows to drive funding decisions.

t: Order Types and Time-in-Force as a Lifecycle
e: Model order-type and time-in-force semantics (limit/market/stop; GTC/IOC/FOK) as a lifecycle.

t: Reconstructing an Order Book from a Market-Data Feed
e: Handle a market-data feed: sequence checking, gap recovery, and snapshot-plus-delta order-book reconstruction.

t: Pre-Trade Risk, Positions, and Real-Time P&L
e: Enforce pre-trade risk limits and keep real-time positions and mark-to-market P&L.

t: Engineering SCA Exemptions Without Wrecking Conversion
e: Decide PSD2 SCA exemptions (low-value, TRA, allowlist) to keep low-risk payments frictionless around 3DS.

t: Engineering DORA Operational Resilience
e: Engineer DORA operational resilience: ICT asset/third-party risk, incident classification, reporting, and resilience testing.

t: Building a FATCA/CRS Tax Reporting Pipeline
e: Classify account tax residency and generate withholding and FATCA/CRS reporting files.

t: Engineering the Collections and Recovery Workflow
e: Model post-delinquency treatment paths: reminders, restructuring, settlement offers, and charge-off/agency handoff.

t: Designing an Identity Verification Pipeline
e: Build a document + liveness/biometric identity-verification pipeline that returns a graded decision.

t: From AML Alert to Filed SAR: Engineering the Case Management Pipeline
e: Turn AML alerts into investigated cases and filed SAR/STR reports, complementing rule-based monitoring.

t: Engineering a Pay-in-4 BNPL Flow
e: Engineer a 4-installment BNPL flow: checkout-time soft credit check, upfront merchant settlement, and installment collection.

t: Engineering a Loan Origination Pipeline
e: Design a loan origination pipeline from application through underwriting, offer, and disbursal.

t: Collateral and LTV Management: Engineering the Loop That Watches Value Slip
e: Track collateral valuation, loan-to-value, margin calls, and liquidation triggers.

t: Variable Recurring Payments and Metered Billing as a Mandate Lifecycle
e: Model variable recurring payments and metered/subscription billing with proration, distinct from retry logic.

t: Building the Issuer Side of a Card Program
e: Build the issuer side: BIN/program config, card production, PIN generation via HSM, and real-time authorization controls.

t: The Card Payment Actors Map: Who Actually Does What
e: One reference map of who does what in a card payment: cardholder, merchant, gateway, acquirer/processor, scheme, issuer, and the settlement return path.

t: Merchant Settlement and Payout: Acquirer Funding
e: From captured transactions to merchant bank account: batching, interchange/scheme-fee deduction, reserves/holdbacks, and T+N funding files.

t: Payment Orchestration: Routing One Charge Across Many PSPs
e: Route a payment across multiple PSPs to maximize auth rate, with health-aware routing, failover, and normalized webhooks.

t: Confirmation of Payee: Checking the Name Before the Money Leaves
e: Name-match the beneficiary before a push payment to stop authorized-push-payment (APP) fraud.

t: Engineering EMVCo QR Payments
e: Encode and decode EMVCo QR payloads (static vs dynamic), handle expiry, and reconcile QR-initiated payments.

t: Dynamic Currency Conversion at the Point of Sale
e: How DCC offers a cardholder their home currency at point of sale, the FX markup and disclosure rules, and settlement implications.

t: Three-Way Reconciliation That Closes the Long Tail
e: Teaches how to build a three-way reconciliation engine (internal ledger vs processor vs bank statement): matching keys and tolerances, break classification, aging, and auto-resolution rules for the long tail.

t: Key Ceremonies and HSM Key Hierarchies for Payments
e: Teaches how to run cryptographic key management for payments: HSM-backed key hierarchies (LMK/ZMK/ZPK), key ceremonies with split knowledge and dual control, rotation, and PIN-block translation.

t: Interbank mTLS and Message Signing
e: Teaches how to secure bank-to-bank and scheme connectivity: mutual TLS with certificate pinning/rotation, detached JWS/XML message signing for non-repudiation, and replay protection with nonces and timestamps.

t: Request to Pay and Mandate Engines
e: How Request to Pay (R2P) messaging works, the standing-mandate lifecycle, consent, and variable recurring payment authorization.

t: Moving Money Across Services Without a Distributed Transaction
e: Teaches how to coordinate a multi-step payment across services without distributed transactions: orchestrated saga steps, compensating actions for partial failures, and guaranteeing money is never stranded.

t: Crediting Crypto Deposits Without Getting Burned by Reorgs
e: Teaches how to safely credit crypto deposits and finalize settlement: confirmation-depth thresholds, mempool/pending tracking, chain-reorg detection and balance rollback, and idempotent handling of replaced transactions.

t: Engineering a Fiat-Backed Stablecoin: Mint, Burn, and the Reserve Invariant
e: Teaches how to engineer a fiat-backed stablecoin: mint-on-deposit / burn-on-redeem flows tied to a reserve ledger, 1:1 reserve invariant checks, and reconciliation between on-chain supply and off-chain custody balances.

t: Stored-Value and E-Money Wallet Ledgers
e: Designing a closed-loop wallet: top-up, hold, spend, refund, safeguarding of e-money, and the double-entry ledger behind a balance.

t: Engineering Treasury Liquidity: Automated Cash Sweeps
e: Teaches how to engineer treasury liquidity: multi-account balance aggregation, target-balance and zero-balance sweep rules, cutoff-aware transfers, and intraday funding checks to keep settlement accounts solvent.

t: Designing a Deterministic Order-Book Matching Engine
e: Teaches how to build a deterministic matching engine: price-time priority order book, limit/market/IOC/FOK order types, single-threaded sequencer for determinism, and gap-free trade/execution event streaming.

t: Building Custody: Hot, Warm, and Cold Wallets Without a Single Point of Compromise
e: Teaches how to architect custody: hot/warm/cold wallet tiers, HSM or MPC key custody, withdrawal approval quorum, address derivation (HD wallets), and sweep flows from deposit to cold storage.

t: Push-to-Card and Instant Disbursements
e: How OCT/push-to-card (Visa Direct, Mastercard Send) moves money to a card in near real time, eligibility/limits, and reversal handling.

t: AP2 vs ACP vs x402 vs Network Tokens: How the Approaches Compare
e: A clear-eyed comparison across trust model, who signs what, payment rails supported, credential handling, settlement, and best-fit use cases.

t: Rules and ML in One Fraud Decision Path
e: Teaches how to combine a deterministic rules engine with an ML risk model in one decision path: rule-precedence and overrides, model score bands, shadow mode, and champion/challenger evaluation with feedback labels.

t: Building a Step-Up Authentication Orchestrator
e: Teaches how to build risk-based step-up auth: an orchestration layer that escalates from silent to OTP/biometric/3DS challenge based on risk signals, with pending-challenge state and resumable transaction context.

t: Building an FX Rate, Spread & Markup Engine
e: Teaches how to build an FX pricing service: ingesting multiple rate feeds, mid-rate derivation, staleness/circuit-breaker handling, per-segment spread/markup, and rate-lock quotes with expiry for customer conversions.

t: Account Updater and the Card-on-File Lifecycle
e: How VAU/ABU keep stored credentials current, credential-on-file mandates, and reducing involuntary churn from expired/reissued cards.

t: MCP, A2A, AP2, and ACP: The Agentic Commerce Protocol Stack
e: How the layers compose: MCP gives an agent tools and context; A2A lets agents talk to each other; AP2/ACP/x402 are the payment rails those agents call when money must move.

t: Engineering the Open Banking Consent Layer: SCA, Scopes, and Token Lifecycles
e: Teaches how to build open-banking APIs: strong customer authentication and exemptions, consent grant/lifecycle, account-information vs payment-initiation scopes, and TPP authorization with token/consent revocation.

t: Engineering a Basel RWA Calculation Engine
e: Teaches the engineering of a risk-weighted-asset calculator: exposure classification, risk-weight lookup (standardized approach), credit-conversion factors for off-balance items, and capital-ratio aggregation for regulatory reporting.

t: Real-Time Velocity Checks and the Fraud Feature Store
e: Teaches how to build low-latency velocity checks: sliding-window counters and aggregates in an online feature store, entity keys (card/device/IP), and consistency between real-time and batch-computed features.

t: Authorization Holds: Incremental, Partial, and Estimated Auth
e: Pre-auth vs estimated vs incremental authorization (hotels, fuel, delivery), partial approvals, and reconciling holds against final capture.

t: Building an Agent-Ready Merchant
e: What a store must expose to sell to agents: a machine-readable product feed/catalog, agentic checkout endpoints, acceptance of delegated payment tokens, idempotency keys for retried agent calls, webhooks for async status…

t: Building an AML Transaction Monitoring Rules Engine
e: Teaches how to build AML transaction monitoring: typology rules (structuring, rapid movement, layering), sliding-window aggregation, alert scoring and deduplication, and case management feeding STR/SAR filing.

t: Implementing the FATF Travel Rule Between VASPs
e: Teaches how to implement the FATF Travel Rule between VASPs: originator/beneficiary PII exchange protocols (IVMS101, TRP/OpenVASP), counterparty VASP discovery, and pre-transfer verification before on-chain send.

t: Resolving Ultimate Beneficial Ownership as a Graph Problem
e: Teaches how to compute ultimate beneficial ownership: modeling ownership as a graph, percentage-through-chain calculation, control vs ownership thresholds, and cycle handling to surface >25% beneficial owners.

t: Stand-In Processing (STIP): Authorizing When the Issuer Is Down
e: How the network authorizes on the issuer's behalf during downtime using stand-in rules and limits, then reconciles advices when the issuer returns.

t: "My Agent Did It": Fraud, Disputes, and Liability in Agentic Commerce
e: The new fraud surface: prompt injection turning a shopping agent into an attacker's buyer, hijacked delegated credentials (Visa saw ~450% more dark-web 'AI Agent' chatter in H1 2026), and disputes when an agent acted on…

t: Delinquency as a State Machine: DPD Buckets, SMA, and NPA Classification
e: Teaches how to model delinquency as a state machine: days-past-due bucket transitions, SMA/NPA classification rules, provisioning triggers, and cure/roll-forward/roll-back logic driven by repayment events.

t: Building a Credit Decisioning Engine
e: Teaches how to build a decisioning engine: feature assembly from bureau/bank/alt data, scorecard vs ML model serving, policy rules and cutoffs, and adverse-action reason-code generation with an audit trail.

t: Building a Sanctions Screening Engine That Controls False Positives
e: Teaches how to build sanctions/watchlist screening: list ingestion (OFAC/UN/EU), transliteration and fuzzy name matching, scoring thresholds, whitelisting, and rescreening on list deltas to control false positives.

t: EMV Cryptograms: ARQC, ARPC, and Offline Data Authentication
e: How the chip generates an ARQC, the issuer validates it and returns an ARPC, plus offline data authentication (SDA/DDA/CDA) and terminal risk management.

t: The Agentic Checkout Flow, End to End
e: A complete walkthrough: product discovery via an AI surface → cart assembly → user approval/mandate → delegated payment token → merchant checkout → authorization → fulfillment → receipts/webhooks.

t: Building a Dunning and Retry Engine for Failed Payments
e: Teaches how to build a smart retry/dunning system: decline-code classification (hard vs soft), backoff and retry-window scheduling, retry-budget limits, and network-token refresh to recover subscription revenue.

t: Building a Deterministic Amortization Schedule Engine
e: Teaches how to compute loan amortization deterministically: EMI/annuity vs reducing-balance formulas, day-count conventions, principal/interest split per installment, and prepayment/rescheduling recalculation.

t: Building a Daily Interest Accrual Engine
e: Teaches how to build a daily interest accrual engine: accrual basis and compounding, accrued-but-unbilled tracking, rate changes mid-period, and idempotent daily accrual jobs that post to the ledger.

t: Agent Identity, Delegation, and Scoped Authorization
e: How a merchant verifies WHICH agent is acting and WHAT it may do.

t: Custody and Asset Servicing Platforms
e: How a custodian holds assets in omnibus vs segregated accounts, the CSD/sub-custodian network, settlement instructions, and asset-servicing (income, proxy, tax).

t: Building Marketplace Split Payments and Connected Payouts
e: Teaches how to architect marketplace money movement: platform vs connected-account balances, fee/commission splits, delayed payouts, negative-balance handling, and merchant-of-record vs facilitator models.

t: Building a Revenue Recognition Engine
e: Teaches how to build a rev-rec engine: performance obligations, deferred-vs-recognized schedules, ratable recognition over time, and how billing events differ from recognition events in the ledger.

t: Engineering Escrow: Conditional Hold and Release with Double-Entry Safety
e: Teaches how to build escrow and conditional hold/release: segregated escrow ledger accounts, release conditions/approvals, partial releases, and expiry auto-refund with double-entry safety.

t: Securities Lending and Repo: Financing the Balance Sheet
e: Loan vs repo mechanics, collateral schedules and haircuts, daily mark-to-market and margin, recalls, and rehypothecation risk.

t: Card Networks Enter Agentic Commerce: Visa Intelligent Commerce and Mastercard Agent Pay
e: How the card networks are adapting tokenization for agents.

t: Chart of Accounts and Sub-Ledger Modeling
e: Teaches how to design a chart of accounts and sub-ledger-to-GL posting model: account hierarchy, dimensions/segments, contra accounts, and how product events map to balanced journal entries.

t: Multi-Currency Accounting and FX Revaluation
e: Teaches how to keep books in multiple currencies with a functional/reporting currency: transaction-date vs settlement-date rates, unrealized/realized FX gain-loss postings, and period-end revaluation runs.

t: Automating the Financial Close
e: Teaches how to automate the financial close: ledger cutoff/freeze, accrual and reversing entries, trial-balance assembly, out-of-balance detection, and soft-close vs hard-close controls.

t: CCP Clearing and Margin: Initial, Variation, and the Default Waterfall
e: Novation to a central counterparty, initial vs variation margin, margin calls, and the default waterfall (margin, default fund, skin-in-the-game).

t: x402: Paying Over HTTP 402 with Stablecoins
e: Coinbase's x402 revives the dormant HTTP 402 Payment Required status code so agents pay for resources machine-to-machine.

t: RTGS vs Deferred Net Settlement
e: Teaches the engineering tradeoffs between gross real-time settlement and deferred net settlement: liquidity vs finality, queue/gridlock resolution in RTGS, and settlement-risk windows in DNS.

t: Nostro/Vostro Reconciliation, From the Ledger Up
e: Teaches how to reconcile correspondent-bank nostro/vostro balances: mirror-account bookkeeping, expected-vs-actual statement (camt.053) matching, value-date breaks, and unreconciled-item aging.

t: Payment-versus-Payment: Settling FX Without Principal Risk
e: Teaches how payment-versus-payment settlement eliminates Herstatt (principal) risk in FX: matched trade submission, pay-in schedules, simultaneous conditional settlement, and pay-out with net funding.

t: Fund Accounting and NAV Calculation
e: How a fund's NAV is struck daily: position keeping, pricing/valuation, accruals, expense amortization, and the striking/publishing pipeline with tolerance checks.

t: ACP: The Agentic Commerce Protocol Behind ChatGPT Instant Checkout
e: The Agentic Commerce Protocol co-developed by Stripe and OpenAI that powers Instant Checkout in ChatGPT.

t: Building a Deterministic Interchange Fee Engine
e: Teaches how to build a deterministic fee engine that classifies each transaction into an interchange category (regulated debit, rewards, CPS qualification) and computes interchange + scheme + acquirer markup for merchant statements.

t: Designing a Netting Engine That Collapses Gross Obligations Into Minimal Settlement
e: Teaches how to build a netting engine that collapses many gross obligations into minimal net settlement positions per counterparty, handling netting cycles, cutoff snapshots, and net-debit-cap enforcement.

t: Modeling Card Chargebacks as a State Machine
e: Teaches how to model the full card dispute lifecycle as a state machine with reason codes, evidence deadlines, representment, pre-arbitration and arbitration, and provisional-credit ledger entries at each transition.

t: Corporate Actions Processing: Dividends, Splits, and Elections
e: The announcement to ex-date to record-date to payment lifecycle for mandatory and voluntary corporate actions, and the entitlement/election engine behind it.

t: Mandates and Verifiable Credentials: Proving an Agent Was Authorized
e: A deep dive on the mandate chain as evidence: verifiable credentials (VCs), signing, the non-repudiable Intent→Cart→Payment chain, revocation and expiry, and why this replaces 'trust me, the user said so' with cryptograp…

t: Card Authorization, Capture, and Clearing: One Transaction, Three Money States
e: Teaches how to model the card transaction as a two-phase (auth then capture) plus clearing/settlement state machine, handling partial captures, incremental auths, auth expiry/reversal, and the auth-vs-settled amount reconciliation.

t: Integrating 3-D Secure 2 Without Breaking Your Checkout
e: Teaches how to integrate 3-D Secure 2: the 3DS Server, Directory Server and issuer ACS handshake, frictionless vs challenge decisioning, device data collection, and liability-shift outcomes feeding the authorization.

t: Network Tokenization and How a Token Vault Shrinks Your PCI-DSS Scope
e: Teaches how a token vault and network tokens (TR-31/EMV payment tokens) remove PAN from application systems, cutting PCI-DSS scope, and how token provisioning, cryptograms, and detokenization boundaries are architected.

t: Smart Order Routing and Best Execution
e: How a buy-side SOR splits a parent order across venues, scores liquidity/fees/latency, and proves best execution with TCA.

t: AP2: Google's Agent Payments Protocol and the Three Mandates
e: Google's open Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

t: Engineering SEPA: Mandates, Sequence Types, and the R-Transaction State Machine
e: Teaches how to engineer SEPA SCT and SDD flows: mandate lifecycle storage, pre-notification timing, FIRST/RCUR sequence types, and the R-transaction taxonomy (reject/return/refund/reversal/revocation) as a state machine.

t: Threading a UETR Through SWIFT MT-to-MX Migration
e: Teaches how to parse legacy MT103/MT202 fields, map them to MX pacs equivalents during coexistence, and thread a gpi UETR end-to-end so a cross-border payment is trackable across correspondent hops.

t: Building for Instant Payments: RTP, FedNow, and Request-for-Payment
e: Teaches how to build for 24x7 irrevocable instant credit: synchronous ISO 20022 request/response, request-for-payment (RfP) flows, credit-transfer timeouts, and idempotent liquidity checks at the rail with no batch cutoff.

t: The FIX Protocol: Engineering a Session and Order Gateway
e: How FIX session layer (logon, heartbeat, sequence-number gap-fill, resend) and application layer (NewOrderSingle, ExecutionReport) actually work, and how to build a resilient FIX engine.

t: Agentic Commerce, Explained
e: What agentic commerce is: AI agents that discover, select, and pay on a user's behalf.

t: Modeling ISO 20022 Payment Messages Without Losing Your Mind
e: Teaches how to model, validate, and generate ISO 20022 XML payment messages (pain.001 initiation, pacs.008 interbank, camt.053 statements) with schema-driven typing, structured references, and idempotent message identifiers.

t: Building a Byte-Level ISO 8583 Codec for Card Authorization
e: Teaches how to build a byte-level ISO 8583 encoder/decoder: primary/secondary bitmaps, data-element (DE) field definitions, MTI parsing, and stan/RRN correlation for card authorization messaging.

t: Building a NACHA ACH File Processor: Records, Hash Totals, and Return Codes
e: Teaches how to build a NACHA file processor: fixed-width file/batch/entry/addenda record hierarchy, hash totals, effective-entry-date windows, and handling R-series return/NOC codes with automated re-presentment logic.

t: Controls, Access, and Testing a System That Moves Money
e: The last mile isn't code — it's who can do what, who approves it, and how you prove it's correct. Segregation of duties, four-eyes, an auditable change trail, and property tests that assert ledger invariants over thousands of scenarios.

t: Reliable Delivery: The Outbox, CDC, and Reconciliation
e: You can't atomically update your database and publish a message. The transactional outbox (or CDC) stops you losing events; reconciliation is how you find and classify the breaks when two systems drift anyway.

t: Consuming APIs and Handling Webhooks
e: Talking to a payment rail is the least reliable part of your system. Treat every outbound call as fallible and reconcile on ambiguity; treat every inbound webhook as hostile — verify, dedupe, ack fast, and go read the truth.

t: Idempotency and Full Resumability
e: The network times out ambiguously, so every request runs zero, one, or many times. Idempotency keys make many behave like one; full resumability lets a crashed money flow resume from its last committed step.

t: Executing Money Flows: Invariants, Reservations, and Overdrafts
e: A transfer is a state machine with money on the line. Model the states explicitly, reserve funds before you commit, enforce invariants at every transition, and decide up front what an overdraft even means.

t: Audit Trails, Event Sourcing, and the GDPR Problem
e: In finance you append, never update or delete. Event sourcing gives a perfect audit trail; the right to be forgotten is where it fights back — and crypto-shredding is how you reconcile the two.

t: The Ledger: Double-Entry Bookkeeping
e: Every transaction is balanced postings that sum to zero — enforce it at write time. The ledger is append-only, and booking, value, and settlement time are three different clocks you must not conflate.

t: Representing Money
e: Never store money in a float. Use integer minor units or fixed-scale decimals, round half-even, allocate so splits sum exactly, and treat currency and the FX rate you used as first-class, auditable data.

t: Give Every Agent Its Own Credential
e: Most teams give a whole multi-agent app one workload identity, so one hijacked agent has every agent's blast radius. Splitting identity across app, cloud, and crypto layers shrinks it to a single role and makes the audit trail provable.

t: Human-in-the-Loop: An Approval Gate on Durable State
e: Series finale, Lesson 7: a sensitive action pauses for human approval, where suspension is just a Lesson 2 checkpoint marked awaiting_approval, the deadline is checked first so a late yes is void, and the action must be idempotent.

t: Policy Is Code, Not a Prompt
e: A system prompt saying never delete records is a suggestion the model can be talked out of. A gateway that returns FORBID for the delete tool cannot. Put enforcement where the model can't reach it and prompt injection stops mattering for access control.

t: Hierarchical Supervision: Bounded Fan-Out, Ordered Fan-In, Fault Isolation
e: Lesson 6: bounded fan-out behind a semaphore, ordered fan-in via a pre-sized results slice, and per-worker fault isolation so one sub-agent panicking becomes one failed result instead of crashing the whole run.

t: "maximum recursion depth exceeded": A Durable-Workflow Checkpointing War Story
e: Threading an SDK client through a checkpointed workflow crashed with maximum recursion depth exceeded. The checkpoint boundary is a serialization boundary: JSON only, values and keys, and anything non-serializable gets injected out-of-band at the composition root.

t: Orchestration and Handoff: Routing Intent to a Specialist
e: Lesson 5: a triage router first-matches a keyword to hand intent to a specialist, and the exact point a substring table stops being able to think.

t: EXHAUSTED Is Not Failure: Bounding Agent Runs
e: The scariest agent failure is the runaway loop that never finishes. Cap every run at max_turns and make EXHAUSTED a first-class outcome, neither a failure nor a silent success, with a typed event stream you can route on.

t: Advanced Memory: Threads, Keyword Retrieval, and Lossy Summarization
e: Lesson 4: memory is three stores, not one — an append-only thread, a keyword knowledge index, and a lossy first-and-last summarizer — and an honest account of where each local stand-in leaks against Azure.

t: Tell the Agent What It's Allowed to Do
e: If your gateway will block a tool call, don't make the agent find out by trying, because each blocked attempt is a wasted turn. A capabilities brief aligns what the model thinks it can do with what enforcement actually allows.

t: Google ADK Glossary: Every Core Concept in One Place
e: The capstone of the series: every core ADK concept defined in one place — agents and orchestration, tools, sessions/state/memory, context and callbacks, runtime and streaming, models, grounding, evaluation, protocols, and deployment.

t: Secure Sandboxing: Running Agent-Written Code Behind a Timeout
e: Lesson 3: run agent-written code behind a hard timeout with exec.CommandContext, distinguish OK from TimedOut, and face the leak — a subprocess is not a security boundary.

t: Governing the Tools You Didn't Write
e: An autonomous harness injects its own tools at runtime, tools that don't exist at build time. Fail-closed governance is only complete when it turns that blind spot into a visible block, then allowlists the known-safe internals deliberately.

t: Agent Config: Defining an ADK Agent in YAML, No Code Required
e: Defining an agent declaratively in YAML and loading it via from_config — the loader reads, resolves, and validates the config into a built agent, so config-as-data works without writing code.

t: Durable Execution: Checkpoint Every Step, Resume After a Crash
e: Lesson 2: a workflow that checkpoints after every step and resumes from the last one after a crash, why at-least-once execution forces idempotent steps, and the atomic-rename store that survives a killed process.

t: Testing Agents Without a Model
e: Put the seam at the router: same interface, a deterministic classifier for tests. The whole orchestration, routing, gateway, human-in-the-loop, and checkpointing, runs in CI with zero API keys and zero network.

t: Context Caching in ADK: Stop Paying for the Same Tokens Every Turn
e: Context caching cuts latency and cost by caching large, stable context — system prompt, reference docs, tool definitions — so repeated calls don't re-send and re-process the same tokens.

t: The LangGraph Glossary: Every Concept in One Place
e: The capstone of the series: every LangGraph concept defined in one place — the graph model, state and reducers, persistence, human-in-the-loop, agents and tools, parallelism, streaming, and the surrounding ecosystem.

t: The Agent Harness: guardrails as middleware around the model
e: Lesson 1: why the input guardrail is a hard block rather than flag-and-pass, why it counts runes instead of bytes, and how a plain net/http handler wraps the (stubbed) model call so it tests with httptest.

t: Azure-Preferred, In-Memory Fallback
e: Same store interface, two implementations: cloud-backed when config exists, in-memory when it doesn't. Don't let a subscription be a hard dependency for make test, it's the ports-and-adapters move teams skip under pressure.

t: Planners & Thinking: Making an ADK Agent Reason Before It Acts
e: Structuring an agent's reasoning: planners that make the model plan-then-act (ReAct-style), the built-in thinking feature, and how a planner improves multi-step tool use over naive prompting.

t: Human-in-the-Loop, Tools, and the Send API
e: The building blocks on top of the core graph: interrupt() to pause for human input, create_react_agent and ToolNode for tool-using agents, and the Send API for dynamic parallel fan-out with a reducer fan-in.

t: AG-UI State Management: The Server
e: The server side of AG-UI state management: middleware emits a DataContent state snapshot from the model's JSON so the client can adopt shared state across turns.

t: Harness Engineering in Go: build the harness, then let Azure supply it
e: Seven patterns that turn a bare model call into production agent infrastructure, each written first as offline Go behind an interface (the seam) so the leap to Azure is a swap, not a rewrite.

t: Most-Restrictive-Wins: Composing Two Layers of Policy
e: An agent can tighten a workload's policy or claim a tool it never mentioned, but it can't loosen an explicit forbid. The subtlety everyone botches: an explicit forbid is a floor, while silence is an absence a tighter layer may fill.

t: Google ADK Code Execution: Let the Agent Run the Code, Not Guess the Answer
e: Letting an agent write and run code: built-in and container-based code executors, safe sandboxed execution, how results flow back into the conversation, and the security tradeoffs.

t: Checkpointing and Persistence: Pause, Resume, Time-Travel
e: A checkpointer saves state at every superstep boundary, so a run can pause, resume on a thread_id, and even fork from an earlier checkpoint (time-travel). This is the foundation human-in-the-loop is built on.

t: AG-UI Human-in-the-Loop: The Server
e: The server side of AG-UI human-in-the-loop: gate a tool with tool.ApprovalRequiredFunc so the server suspends the run and resumes on the client's decision.

t: An Eval Regression Gate in CI
e: Agent systems rot because nobody catches quality regressions until users do. A committed baseline plus a gate that fails the build turns the agents got worse into a red X and a reviewable diff in the pull request.

t: Skills: Packaging Agent Capabilities as Reusable, Discoverable Bundles

e: Google's A2A spec standardises how agents talk to other agents (not just tools). The Go client is small; the conceptual shift is what matters.

t: Google Cloud's 12 agent design patterns — mapped to real...
e: Google publishes a 12-pattern taxonomy for agent design. Most of them have direct corollaries in production code; one or two are best ignored. The mapping I've used.

t: Saga rollback when half the steps succeeded — the...
e: A saga is fine when every step succeeds. The interesting code is what runs when step 3 of 5 fails and you have to undo 1 and 2 in the right order. The patterns I use.

t: Cost-aware agent dispatch — when the cheap agent is enough
e: Not every query needs the production agent. A cost-aware dispatcher decides whether to route to the cheap-and-fast agent or the expensive-and-thorough one. Same UX, dramatically lower bill.

t: Latency-aware agent dispatch — picking by SLO, not by...
e: Two agents can do the same job. One takes 200ms; the other takes 5 seconds. Pick by user-facing SLO, not by which agent is "better." The dispatcher pattern.

t: The case for boring stack choices in regulated AI
e: Postgres over the latest vector DB. Go stdlib over the framework du jour. Single binary over Kubernetes operator. The choices that bore reviewers and delight on-call engineers.

t: Default-to-Prototype as a culture, not just a flag
e: An agent that doesn't declare a tier defaults to Prototype, not Production. The flag is the code; the culture is what enforces "new code is not production until someone says so."

t: embed.FS as a deployment unit — config, prompts, UI assets
e: Go's embed.FS bundles files into the binary at compile time. The pattern collapses what would be a multi-artefact deploy into one binary. Three places it pays back daily.

t: GOMEMLIMIT and the soft GC pacing change every Go...
e: GOMEMLIMIT tells the Go runtime to keep memory below a soft cap by running GC harder when it's close. For containers with hard memory limits, this prevents OOM kills. The setting every Go service in K8s should have.

t: Egress costs — the gotcha that kills cloud-arbitrage plans
e: Cross-cloud data movement is billed by the GB. The bill is invisible until it isn't. A multi-region or multi-cloud architecture that doesn't model egress costs in design will discover them in production.

t: Data residency in the Gulf — UAE ADGM/DIFC + Saudi SAMA...
e: An open-banking platform serving UAE and Saudi customers had to honour three overlapping regulators: three overlapping Middle East regulators. Notes on the architecture that satisfied all three.

t: GKE for stateful AI workloads — the patterns that...
e: Multi-agent stacks have state: vector indexes, chat histories, agent memory. GKE for AI workloads needs StatefulSets, PVCs, gateway controllers, and the patterns that work in 2026.

t: UPI integration — the spec quirks no one mentions
e: UPI is the most popular payment rail in India. The spec is precise. The implementation guides are not. Notes on the integration details that ate weeks the first time.

t: KYC under the RBI Master Direction vs Aadhaar offline...
e: Two KYC pathways an Indian fintech has to support. The Master Direction (Video KYC, etc.) and Aadhaar Offline KYC. Different speeds, different evidence requirements, different audit shapes.

t: Voice AI for two-wheelers — multi-language patterns from...
e: A rider asks the bike a question in Marathi, Hindi, or English. The voice stack has to do ASR, intent classification, dispatch to a service tool, generate a response, TTS — all under 3 seconds. Notes from the proof-of-concept.

t: Brownlow — Cloud KMS + Security Command Center for vote...
e: Vote integrity needed two things the platform team couldn't fake even by accident: signing keys we couldn't access, and continuous security monitoring we couldn't silence. KMS + SCC delivered both.

t: AIGP body of knowledge — a Go engineer's reading map
e: IAPP's AI Governance Professional certification covers a body of knowledge worth knowing whether you certify or not. The mapping from BOK to working Go code for the engineer who wants to understand AI governance practically.

t: The board policy is not a slide — it's a YAML file
e: The bank's board approves an AI policy. The policy exists as a slide deck nobody reads. The risk team's actual operational policy is what's in the code. Closing that gap is the FREE-AI Rec 14 win.

t: Audit logs are the API of record
e: The audit log isn't a side effect of the system. It's the contract you owe to regulators, customers, and your future self. Treat it as a first-class API — schema, versioning, and SLOs included.

t: Twelve Go idioms I changed my mind about
e: Patterns I confidently recommended five years ago that I'd argue against today. The list of "things you used to do in Go that don't pay back anymore."

t: iter.Seq — the pull iterator pattern in Go 1.23+
e: Range-over-function landed in Go 1.23. `iter.Seq` lets you write iterators that compose. The patterns that pay back; the ones that don't.

t: errgroup patterns for parallel agent dispatch
e: Fan out to N agents; first error cancels the rest; collect successful results. errgroup is the right tool for this; the patterns are concise but worth getting exactly right.

t: Twelve months of writing in public — what worked, what...
e: Reflections on a year of consistent technical writing. The post categories that compounded; the ones that didn't; what I'd tell someone starting out.

t: The recruiter test — what your repo says before the...
e: A recruiter spends 90 seconds on your GitHub before deciding to talk to you. What they're looking for; what makes them skip; what signals matter more than the README.

t: Twelve months of Genie in production — what survived,...
e: An honest retrospective on the open-source Genie project after a year. The patterns that held up; the ones we rebuilt; the code we deleted because it solved problems we didn't actually have.
